kind: OS service supervision and descriptor custody tools

runtime.execution: Small independent Unix processes communicate through service-directory controls, event FIFOs and Unix sockets.
runtime.service_boundary: Operator/OS daemon supervisor, outside the refitting agent; shared services should not be paused by their consumer.

summary: Stop/continue, readiness, independent logging and file-descriptor custody clarify what an outpost/refit must coordinate versus delegate to OS services.

inspection.scope: Read supervisor signal/state dispatch, readiness, control CLI, fd-holder and log contracts, and available test runner.
inspection.limits: No populated src/tests suite in snapshot and no daemon executed; downstream service protocols and complete logger implementation not audited.

actions.name: s6-svc

actions.lifecycle: Control and readiness are distinct; non-listening supervisor reports error.

actions.name: s6-fdholder store/retrieve/list/getdump/setdump
actions.input: FD, identity, expiration and transfer operation
actions.lifecycle: Independent daemon survives client replacement; its death loses held FDs absent transfer.

actions.name: s6-log
actions.input: Input stream and logging script/flush/line options
actions.lifecycle: Independent logger; line processing changes framing by configured defaults.

evidence.claim: STOP/CONT target process or process group and update pause status; reload sends configured signal.
Supervisor dispatch table separates lifecycle states; notification updates ready stamp/state and broadcasts event.
CLI can wait on service events or write control bytes; supervisor-not-listening is distinct error.
Separate daemon stores/retrieves/transfers FDs; descriptors are lost if daemon dies without transfer.
Line logger has blocking flush mode, default line splitting and partial-line termination timeout; supplied text stream is the scope.
Runner compares stdout with expected/baseline data and rejects missing baseline; underlying src/tests absent here.

strengths: Standing services and descriptor custody can remain independent of a harness rebuild.
Readiness, paused state and restart are distinct observable operations.
limits: STOP targets process/group; it does not settle in-flight provider requests or serialize application work.
A consumer refit must not stop shared service daemons; the FD holder itself needs separate continuity.
arconaut_questions: Which resources belong to the agent/outpost, and which belong to independently supervised services?
What exact settled/paused state must be checked before refit rather than inferred from supervisor acknowledgement?
